title: Visual regression run manifest
description: A machine-readable record of every screenshot comparison made during a test run, written by a visual regression tool and read by CI tooling (PR comment bots, review dashboards, approval tools). Runner-agnostic: everything specific to the test runner lives in `runner`. The envelope, the CI block and the open `extra` objects follow CTRF (ctrf.io) naming so a manifest maps onto a CTRF report without loss; see the `toCtrf`/`fromCtrf` converters. Consumers must ignore keys they do not know.

reportFormat.description: Identifies the document as a visual regression manifest (CTRF has `reportFormat: "CTRF"`).

specVersion.description: Version of this format (semver). The major is bumped on breaking changes only; readers accept every version with the major they know.

updatedAt.description: When the file was last written (ISO 8601). Writers rewrite the file after every comparison, so a manifest is complete even when the run was aborted.

projectRoot.description: Absolute path (on the machine that ran the tests) that every relative path in the manifest resolves against. Not necessarily the repository root: `ci.workspace` is the checkout directory.

ci.description: CI metadata detected from environment variables. `null` outside CI, `{ "provider": null }` when only a generic `CI` flag was set.

options.description: Global tool options as configured, in the writer's vocabulary (for the Cypress plugin: every `pluginVisualRegression*` option with the prefix stripped).

status.description: `passed`: within the limits. `failed`: over the limits, `.actual` and `.diff` images kept for review. `missing-baseline`: no baseline and the tool was told not to create one. `created`: no baseline, the actual image became the baseline. `updated`: the baseline was overwritten on request. `approved`: the baseline was replaced from a review UI. `failed` and `missing-baseline` are the entries that need a human. In CTRF terms `missing-baseline` is `failed` and `created`, `updated`, `approved` are `passed`, with the manifest status kept in `rawStatus`.

tool.description: What wrote the manifest: a visual regression plugin, a converter, a review tool. Same shape as CTRF's `tool`.

summary.description: Counts over `entries`, so a consumer can tell whether a human is needed without reading them all. Writers recompute it on every write; readers merging several manifests recompute it from the merged entries.

platform.description: The machine that ran the tests (the host), which is not necessarily the device under test: for a mobile or remote-device run see the entries' `target`. Named like CTRF's `environment`: `osPlatform` is an open string (Node-based writers use `process.platform` names: `linux`, `darwin`, `win32`), `osRelease` the kernel release, `osVersion` the human-readable OS version.

target.description: What was captured, for tools that are not a browser: a desktop or mobile application on a device, an emulator or a remote farm. Everything is optional; unknown keys are allowed.

density.description: Device pixels per logical pixel (scale factor / dpr).

ci.description: Where the run happened. Keys that have a CTRF `environment` equivalent carry its name (`commit`, `branchName`, `repositoryName`, `repositoryUrl`, `buildId`, `buildName`, `buildNumber`, `buildUrl`); the rest is what CTRF lacks.

provider.description: Known values: `github`, `gitlab`. Other CI systems are free-form lowercase ids; `null` when only a generic CI flag was set.

commit.description: On GitHub `pull_request` events this is the synthetic merge commit; tools that write to the PR branch must use `pullRequest.headSha`.

buildId.description: The run or pipeline id (GitHub `GITHUB_RUN_ID`, GitLab `CI_PIPELINE_ID`); locates the artifacts together with `runAttempt`.

buildUrl.description: Link to the run or job page.

workspace.description: Absolute path of the checked-out repository on the CI machine.

runner.description: What ran the tests (Cypress, Playwright, a mobile driver), as opposed to `tool`, which wrote the manifest. Only `name` is required; the remaining keys are runner vocabulary and writers may add their own.

specs.description: Test files of the run relative to `projectRoot`, when known up front.

cloud.description: Hosted runner dashboard details, when recording.

upload.description: Where the images and snapshots of the run were uploaded to, when an upload service was used.

path.description: Relative to `projectRoot`, `/` separators; `null` when the file does not exist. Baseline, actual and diff of an entry share one extension (PNG for all current writers); `.actual` and `.diff` go before it.

attachment.description: Any other file an entry wants to point at (a trace, a video, a DOM snapshot). Same shape as a CTRF attachment; `path` is relative to `projectRoot`.

subject.description: What the screenshot is a picture of, as opposed to the test that took it: a component story, a page, a screen. Tool-neutral; the id is whatever the producer uses to name the thing (for example a Storybook story id), so tools can group or match entries by it.

extra.description: Open metadata keyed by namespace, like CTRF's `extra`; every value is an object. Consumers must ignore namespaces they do not know. Conventional namespaces on an entry or image: `design` (a design software source: `tool`, `file`, `node`, `version`, for example the Figma file, frame and version a baseline was exported from) and `storybook` (`args`, `globals`). `visualRegression` is reserved for the CTRF converters. Nothing here takes part in baseline identity.

renderer.description: Where the pixels came from, as opposed to `platform`, which is where the test ran. Entries with different renderers are different baselines.

backend.description: Known values: `native` (the test runner's own capture), `docker`, `cloud`. Writers may add their own, e.g. `device` or `emulator`.

name.description: What rendered the pixels: a browser, an app or a device. Absent when `backend` says enough.

browser.description: Browser name; kept for browser renderers, same as `name`.

rendererVersion.description: Version of the renderer image; absent under `native`.

imageDigest.description: Content digest of the renderer image; absent under `native`.

entryOptions.description: The comparison options the entry was made with, exactly as configured (`imagesPath` keeps its tokens unexpanded).

screenshotConfig.description: Capture options in the runner's vocabulary (Cypress `screenshot` config); JSON-serializable keys only.

entry.description: One screenshot comparison. Maps onto a CTRF test of `type: "visual"`: `name` is the test name, `test.titlePath` without its last element the suite, `test.filePath` the file path, `message` the message, `duration` the duration.

name.description: Screenshot name, equal to the baseline file stem. Unique within a run.

filePath.description: Test file relative to `projectRoot`, `/` separators. Empty when unknown.

titlePath.description: Describe blocks and test title, outermost first.

retry.description: Attempt index of the test this comparison belongs to: `0` for the first attempt (CTRF's `retries` is a count, not an index).

diffRatio.description: Share of differing pixels, 0..1. `0` when no comparison ran.

maxDiffRatio.description: Largest `diffRatio` the comparison accepts, 0..1. A pixel-count limit (`maxDiffPixels`, ...) is stored as a ratio of the image size; when both kinds were set, the stricter one. Absent when the writer does not know it. `status` stays the source of truth for the outcome: a ratio computed from a count can disagree with the tool at the boundary.

colorThreshold.description: Per-pixel color tolerance the comparison used, on the scale `colorMetric` names.

colorMetric.description: The color distance `colorThreshold` is measured in; required with it. `yiq`: pixelmatch's weighted YIQ delta, 0..1. `resemble`: Resemble.js's per-channel tolerance. `deltaE`: CIEDE2000. Other values are allowed.

baseline.description: The baseline path is always known, even when the file does not exist yet (`missing-baseline`).

baselineWritten.description: `true` whenever the baseline file was (re)written during the run, whatever the status.

duration.description: How long the capture and comparison took, in milliseconds, when the writer measured it.

platform.description: Where this screenshot was taken; per entry because manifests of several machines get merged.

browser.description: Absent for non-browser targets (desktop and mobile apps).

variant.description: Producer-chosen id that tells entries of the same screenshot name apart (device, OS version, density, locale, theme, project, ...). Part of the baseline identity when merging manifests; absent, identity falls back to `platform.osPlatform` + `platform.browser.name` + renderer.

hashes.description: sha256 of the files listed in `images`; a key is present only when the file exists.
